items.stem: 자연스러운 대화가 되도록 <보기>의 ⓐ~ⓓ를 올바르게 배열한 것은?
items.box:
A: Jiho, let's decide what to cook for dinner.
B: Okay. Do you have anything in mind?
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
<보기>
ⓐ B: I don't agree with you. It's not that hard. Pizza and spaghetti are easy to make.
ⓑ A: Hmm, which do you prefer, Italian food or Korean food?
ⓒ A: Italian food? But cooking Italian food is difficult.
ⓓ B: I prefer Italian food to Korean food.
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
A: Great! Then let's make them. I'll help you!
items.explain:
저녁 메뉴를 정하자는 말에 B가 "Do you have anything in mind?"라고 하자 A가 "Hmm, which do you prefer, Italian food or Korean food?"(ⓑ)로 선호를 묻고, B가 "I prefer Italian food to Korean food."(ⓓ)라고 답한다.
A가 "Italian food? But cooking Italian food is difficult."(ⓒ)라고 하자 B가 "I don't agree with you. It's not that hard. Pizza and spaghetti are easy to make."(ⓐ)로 반박하고, A의 "Great! Then let's make them."으로 이어진다. 따라서 ⓑ-ⓓ-ⓒ-ⓐ.
wrong: ② 어렵다는 말(ⓒ)이 이탈리아 음식을 고른 답(ⓓ)보다 먼저 온다.
③ 선호를 묻기(ⓑ) 전에 답(ⓓ)이 온다.
④ 반박(ⓐ)이 그 대상인 ⓒ보다 먼저 온다.
⑤ Italian food? 라는 되물음(ⓒ)이 그 답을 듣기 전에 나온다.

box.title: <보기>
lines: ㄱ. I wonder where are you from.
ㄴ. Caffeine will keep you awake at night.
ㄷ. I don't know how this machine works.
ㄹ. Bob wants to practice me the piano.
ㅁ. Wearing a helmet will keep you safety.
ㅂ. Did you see her carrying the box by herself?

choices: ㄱ, ㄹ
ㄴ, ㄷ
ㄴ, ㄷ, ㅂ
ㄱ, ㅁ, ㅂ
ㄴ, ㄷ, ㄹ, ㅂ
items.explain:
ㄴ "Caffeine will keep you awake"(keep + 목적어 + 형용사), ㄷ "I don't know how this machine works."(간접의문문 어순), ㅂ "Did you see her carrying the box"(지각동사 + 목적어 + -ing)는 옳다.
ㄱ where are you from → where you are from(간접의문문 어순), ㄹ practice me → me to practice(want + 목적어 + to부정사), ㅁ safety(명사) → safe(형용사 보어)로 고쳐야 한다. 따라서 ㄴ, ㄷ, ㅂ.
wrong: ① ㄱ·ㄹ 모두 틀린 문장이다.
② ㅂ도 옳은 문장이므로 빠져서는 안 된다.
④ ㄱ·ㅁ은 틀린 문장이다.
⑤ ㄹ Bob wants to practice me → wants me to practice.

items.box:
B: Mom, many buses stop here.
W: That's true. We should be careful not to take the wrong bus.
B: Which bus do we have to take?
W: We should take bus number 270.
B: Okay, Mom. How long will it take to get to the museum?
W: It'll take about 30 minutes.
B: The name of the stop is National Science Museum, right?
W: Yes, ______________(A)______________
B: Oh, I got it.
choices: don't forget to prepare your bus card.
let's take the subway together.
I prefer the bus to the subway.
it'll take more than an hour by subway.
first, sign up for our app.
items.explain: 엄마가 "We should be careful not to take the wrong bus."라며 버스 타는 것을 안내하고, 정류장 이름을 확인한 아들에게 "Yes," 하고 덧붙이는 당부이므로 버스 카드를 준비하라는 ① "don't forget to prepare your bus card."가 알맞다. 아들의 "Oh, I got it."과도 이어진다.
wrong: ② 버스를 타기로 한 대화에서 지하철을 타자는 말은 어긋난다.
③ 버스와 지하철의 선호를 말하는 대사로 흐름에 맞지 않는다.
④ 지하철 소요 시간은 이 대화와 관계없다.
⑤ 앱 가입은 자전거 대여 대화의 대사이다.

choices:
A: Which do you prefer, team sports or individual sports?
B: I prefer team sports to individual sports.

A: Why is that?
B: Because math has clear answers to problems.

A: Do you know how to cook tomato spaghetti?
B: I don't agree with you. It's not that hard.

A: What's next?
B: Then, mix them with tomato sauce, and add a little salt.

A: Ellen, what classes do we have in the afternoon?
B: Let me see. We have math and science classes.
items.explain: "Do you know how to cook tomato spaghetti?"는 조리법을 아느냐는 물음이므로 "Sure. First, …"처럼 방법을 설명해야 한다. ③의 "I don't agree with you. It's not that hard."는 상대의 의견에 반대하는 말이라 어색하다.
wrong: ① 선호를 묻고 I prefer team sports to individual sports. 로 답한다.
② 이유를 묻고 Because … 로 답한다.
④ 다음 단계를 묻고 Then, … 으로 답한다.
⑤ 오후 수업을 묻고 math and science 라고 답한다.

lines: Reporter: Mr. Davis. Do you like your job as a sports agent?
Mr. Davis: Yes. I love sports, and I enjoy everything about business. I think my job is perfect for me.
Reporter: Can you tell me more about your job?

Mr. Davis: When my clients have a new contract to sign, I check it carefully. I do my best to ⓐ<u>make the contract fair</u> for them. Also, I often receive phone calls from advertising companies. They want my clients in their advertisements. Then, I try to get the best deal for my clients.

items.stem: Mr. Davis에 대한 설명으로 올바르지 <u>않은</u> 것은?
choices: Mr. Davis is satisfied with his job.
Mr. Davis carefully checks new contracts for his clients.
Mr. Davis tries to make contracts fair for his clients.
Advertising companies want Mr. Davis to appear in their advertisements.
Mr. Davis tries to get the best deals for his clients rather than for advertising companies.
items.explain:
[지문 요지] 스포츠 에이전트 Mr. Davis는 스포츠와 사업을 모두 좋아하며 고객의 계약서를 꼼꼼히 확인해 공정하게 만들고 광고 회사와 최선의 조건을 협상한다.
본문 "They want my clients in their advertisements."에서 광고 회사가 원하는 것은 Davis가 아니라 그의 고객들이다. ④는 틀리다.
items.source: L5 본문 2대목 Mr. Davis · 통합본 L5 p.39 T/F · p.57 21번
wrong: ① I think my job is perfect for me. 와 일치한다.
② I check it carefully. 와 일치한다.
③ make the contract fair for them 과 일치한다.
⑤ I try to get the best deal for my clients. 와 일치한다.

items.stem: <보기>에서 윗글의 ⓐ와 문법적으로 성격이 같은 것<u>만</u>으로 짝지어진 것은?

box.title: <보기>
lines: ㄱ. Wearing a helmet will keep you safe.
ㄴ. She found the book boring.
ㄷ. I make sure everything goes well.
ㄹ. Sitting under the tree kept us cool.
ㅁ. Exercise made her healthy.
ㅂ. He took a shot at the goal, but it missed.

choices: ㄱ, ㄴ
ㄷ, ㅂ
ㄱ, ㄴ, ㄹ
ㄱ, ㄴ, ㄹ, ㅁ
ㄴ, ㄷ, ㄹ, ㅁ
items.explain:
ⓐ "make the contract fair"는 「make + 목적어 + 형용사(목적격 보어)」로 '계약을 공정하게 만들다'는 뜻이다.
ㄱ keep you safe, ㄴ found the book boring, ㄹ kept us cool, ㅁ made her healthy 는 모두 목적어 뒤에 형용사 보어가 온 같은 구조이다.
ㄷ make sure (that) everything goes well 은 「make sure + 절」(반드시 ~하게 하다)이고, ㅂ took a shot 은 3형식이다.
items.source: 학습지 p.8 A-4·B-1, p.7 예문 · 학습지 p.6·p.1 문장
wrong: ① ㄹ·ㅁ도 같은 구조이므로 빠져서는 안 된다.
② ㄷ·ㅂ은 목적격 보어가 없다.
③ ㅁ도 같은 구조이므로 빠져서는 안 된다.
⑤ ㄷ make sure 는 5형식이 아니다.

lines: remove_all_plz
(…) I apologized to him, and I deleted my post immediately. However, the copies still remain online. I want to remove them all. Please help me.
Happy_Digital_Laundry

We removed all the copies online, ____ⓐ____ some copies may remain on personal devices. ____ⓑ____ you see the copies again, please contact us. ____ⓒ____ you share things online, be careful. Remember that sharing something online is easy, but removing it is hard.

choices: Happy Digital Laundry completely erased every copy from all devices.
Some copies may still remain on personal devices.
Remember that sharing something online is hard, but removing it is easy.
We removed all the copies on personal devices, but some copies may remain online.
Happy Digital Laundry will contact Bella if they find more copies.
items.explain:
[지문 요지] 사본을 지워 달라는 Bella의 부탁에 Happy Digital Laundry가 온라인 사본은 지웠지만 개인 기기에는 남아 있을 수 있다고 답하며, 온라인 공유는 쉽지만 지우기는 어렵다고 당부한다.
본문 "some copies may remain on personal devices"와 ②가 일치한다.
items.source: L6 본문 2대목 Laundry 답장 1 · 통합본 L6 p.38 T/F · 실전모의고사 21번
wrong: ① 모든 기기에서 완전히 지운 것이 아니다.
③ sharing … is easy, but removing it is hard — 반대로 되어 있다.
④ 지운 곳은 online 이고 남을 수 있는 곳이 personal devices 이다.
⑤ 사본을 다시 보면 Bella가 연락하라(please contact us)고 했다.

items.explain:
ⓐ 온라인 사본은 지웠'지만' 개인 기기에는 남을 수 있다 → but, ⓑ '만약' 사본을 다시 본다면 연락하라 → If, ⓒ 온라인에 공유할 '때' 조심하라 → When.
원문: "We removed all the copies online, but some copies may remain on personal devices. If you see the copies again, please contact us. When you share things online, be careful."
wrong: ② and 는 지웠다는 말과 남아 있다는 말을 대조하지 못한다.
③ Because you see the copies again 은 뜻이 통하지 않는다.
④ so·Although 는 흐름과 맞지 않는다.
⑤ Because you share things online, be careful 은 어색하다.

choices: What do you advise me doing?
She saw chasing the puppy its tail.
Did he ask she to bring a camera?
The teacher didn't allow us talked during the test.
I saw him entering the classroom.
items.explain: ⑤ "I saw him entering the classroom."은 「지각동사 see + 목적어 + 현재분사」로 옳다.
wrong: ① advise me doing → advise me to do(advise + 목적어 + to부정사).
② saw chasing the puppy → saw the puppy chasing(목적어 뒤에 보어).
③ ask she → ask her(목적격).
④ allow us talked → allow us to talk(allow + 목적어 + to부정사).

lines: Reporter: Hello, Ms. Ali. Can you tell me why you became a sports journalist?
Ms. Ali: Well, I've always had a passion for sports and writing. Writing about sports makes me ____ⓐ____.
Reporter: There was a big baseball game yesterday. How did you spend the day?

Ms. Ali: I arrived at the baseball park early. Before the game started, I had an interview with the players. I took a lot of notes during the game. After the game, I went to the press conference with other journalists. I asked the players how they felt about the game. In the afternoon, I had to write an article and edit it very quickly. My article ____ⓑ____ online. I love writing about sports.

choices: Why did Ms. Ali decide to become a sports journalist?
Did Ms. Ali arrive at the baseball park after the game started?
Did Ms. Ali interview the players before the game?
Which team won the baseball game?
Did Ms. Ali go to a press conference by herself after the game?
items.explain:
[지문 요지] 스포츠 기자 Ms. Ali의 하루 — 경기 전 인터뷰, 경기 중 메모, 경기 후 기자회견, 오후 기사 작성.
④ 야구 경기에서 '어느 팀이 이겼는지'는 글에 나오지 않는다.
items.source: L5 본문 1대목 Ms. Ali · 학습지 p.6 Details 4 · 통합본 L5 p.38 T/F
wrong: ① I've always had a passion for sports and writing. 으로 답할 수 있다.
② I arrived at the baseball park early. → No 로 답할 수 있다.
③ Before the game started, I had an interview with the players. → Yes.
⑤ with other journalists → No 로 답할 수 있다.

items.explain:
ⓐ 「make + 목적어 + 형용사」에서 '나'가 신나는 감정을 느끼므로 과거분사형 형용사 excited, ⓑ 기사는 '게시되는' 대상이므로 수동태 과거 was posted.
원문: "Writing about sports makes me excited. … My article was posted online."
wrong: ② exciting 은 '신나게 하는'으로 사람의 감정에 쓰지 않으며 posted 는 능동이다.
③ posted 는 능동으로 기사가 무언가를 게시했다는 뜻이 된다.
④ excitedly 는 부사라 보어가 될 수 없다.
⑤ exciting 은 사람이 느끼는 감정에 쓰지 않는다.

lines: Last month, I received an email from an unknown name. I clicked on the link in the email, and a website showed up. I ____ⓐ____ the website immediately, but I felt something was ____ⓑ____. My computer became very ____ⓒ____. I asked the computer store to check my computer, and they found that someone added bad programs through the link. These programs made my computer slow.

choices: The writer clicked on the link in the email, and no website showed up.
The writer closed the website immediately, but he felt something was right.
The writer asked the computer store to check his computer, and they found that nobody added bad programs through the link.
Last month, the writer received an email from an unknown name.
The writer asked his friend to check his computer, and they found that someone added bad programs through the link.
items.explain:
[지문 요지] 모르는 사람의 이메일 링크를 눌렀다가 컴퓨터가 느려졌고, 컴퓨터 가게에서 링크를 통해 나쁜 프로그램이 설치되었음을 알아냈다는 글이다.
④는 첫 문장 "Last month, I received an email from an unknown name."과 그대로 일치한다.
wrong: ① a website showed up — 웹사이트가 떴다.
② something was wrong — right 가 아니다.
③ someone added bad programs — nobody 가 아니다.
⑤ 친구가 아니라 the computer store 에 부탁했다.

items.explain:
ⓐ 웹사이트를 즉시 '닫았다' → closed, ⓑ 뭔가 '잘못된' 느낌 → wrong, ⓒ 컴퓨터가 매우 '느려졌다' → slow.
원문: "I closed the website immediately, but I felt something was wrong. My computer became very slow." 뒤의 "These programs made my computer slow."에서도 확인된다.
wrong: ② 웹사이트가 이미 떴으므로 다시 opened 할 수 없다.
③ right·fast 는 문제가 생긴 흐름과 반대이다.
④ fine·fast 는 흐름과 반대이다.
⑤ 마지막 문장 made my computer slow 와 어긋난다.

lines: Hello. Today, I'll introduce a special app, MuzSearch. When you want to know the title of a song, this app will help you. It's simple to use. First, open the MuzSearch app and touch the search icon. Second, press the microphone icon and wait for a while. Then the app will show the title on the screen. If you like the song, don't forget to press the heart icon. The song ____ⓐ____ to your favorites. Try it now!

choices: A Special App, MuzSearch
Wait for a While
Press the Microphone Icon
Touch the Search Icon
Your Favorites
items.explain:
[지문 요지] 노래 제목을 찾아 주는 앱 MuzSearch의 사용법을 소개하는 글이다.
첫 문장 "Today, I'll introduce a special app, MuzSearch."가 글 전체의 주제이므로 제목은 ① 'A Special App, MuzSearch'가 알맞다.
wrong: ② 잠시 기다리라는 것은 한 단계일 뿐이다.
③ 마이크 아이콘을 누르는 것은 한 단계일 뿐이다.
④ 검색 아이콘을 누르는 것은 한 단계일 뿐이다.
⑤ 즐겨찾기는 마지막 부분의 세부 내용이다.

choices: save
saved
will save
will be saved
is saving
items.explain:
노래(The song)는 '저장되는' 대상이고 앞으로의 일이므로 미래 수동태 「will be + 과거분사」 will be saved 가 알맞다.
원문: "The song will be saved to your favorites."
wrong: ① save(능동 현재)는 노래가 무언가를 저장한다는 뜻이 된다.
② saved 는 능동 과거이다.
③ will save 는 능동이다.
⑤ is saving 은 진행형 능동이다.

box.title: <보기>
lines: ⓐ a notice, short film, etc. that promotes a product, service, event, etc.
ⓑ to make changes to data or text by correcting mistakes and making improvements
ⓒ the series of jobs that a person has in a particular field of work
ⓓ facts or information, especially when used to find out things or to make decisions
ⓔ an attempt to score a goal in a game

choices: The (      ) showed a new smartphone.
I have to (      ) some video clips.
She hopes to have a successful (      ) in music.
He took a (      ) at the goal, but it missed.
The judge made a (      ) decision.
items.explain:
영영풀이: ⓐ '상품·서비스를 홍보하는 공지나 짧은 영상' → advertisement(광고), ⓑ '오류를 고치고 개선해 자료나 글을 바꾸다' → edit(편집하다), ⓒ '한 분야에서 한 사람이 거치는 직업의 과정' → career(경력), ⓓ '판단에 쓰이는 사실이나 정보' → data(자료), ⓔ '경기에서 득점하려는 시도' → shot(슛).
⑤ "The judge made a (      ) decision."에는 fair(공정한)가 들어가야 하는데 <보기>에 없다.
items.source: 학습지 p.2·p.11 크로스워드 영영풀이 · p.1 예문 1·11·6·17·12
wrong: ① The advertisement showed a new smartphone.
② edit some video clips(영상을 편집하다).
③ a successful career in music(음악 분야의 성공적인 경력).
④ took a shot at the goal(골을 향해 슛을 쏘다).

items.stem: 자연스러운 대화가 되도록 <보기>의 ⓐ~ⓓ를 올바르게 배열한 것은?
items.box:
G: We have math and English classes today.
B: Right. Sora, which do you prefer, math or English?
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
<보기>
ⓐ B: Why is that?
ⓑ G: Because math has clear answers to problems. How about you?
ⓒ G: I prefer math to English.
ⓓ B: I like English better. I'm not good at math.
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
items.explain:
B가 "which do you prefer, math or English?"라고 물었으므로 G가 "I prefer math to English."(ⓒ)로 답하고, B가 "Why is that?"(ⓐ)으로 이유를 묻는다.
G가 "Because math has clear answers to problems. How about you?"(ⓑ)로 답하며 되묻자 B가 "I like English better. I'm not good at math."(ⓓ)로 답한다. 따라서 ⓒ-ⓐ-ⓑ-ⓓ.
wrong: ② 이유(ⓑ)가 이유를 묻는 말(ⓐ)보다 먼저 온다.
③ 선호를 말하기(ⓒ) 전에 Why is that?(ⓐ)이 온다.
④ How about you?(ⓑ)가 그 답(ⓓ)보다 뒤에 온다.
⑤ B의 답(ⓓ)이 G의 답보다 먼저 나온다.

lines: Dear Big Digital Manager,

(A) I ⓐ<u>bought</u> Bluetooth headphones from your site last month. (B) However, music only comes out of one side, and the other side ⓑ<u>doesn't</u> work. (C) I don't know ⓒ<u>what is the problem</u> or what ⓓ<u>to do</u>. (D) I hope ⓔ<u>to hear</u> from you soon. (E)
Best,
Jun Park

items.explain:
간접의문문은 「의문사 + 주어 + 동사」 어순이므로 ⓒ "what is the problem"은 "what the problem is"로 고쳐야 한다. "I don't know what the problem is or what to do."
나머지는 옳다: ⓐ bought(last month, 과거), ⓑ the other side doesn't work(3인칭 단수 부정), ⓓ what to do(의문사 + to부정사), ⓔ hope to hear(hope + to부정사).
items.source: L6 Present Your Ideas — In Writing 이메일
wrong: ① last month 가 있으므로 과거 bought 가 옳다.
② 주어 the other side 가 단수이므로 doesn't 가 옳다.
④ what to do 는 '무엇을 해야 할지'로 옳다.
⑤ hope 는 to부정사를 목적어로 취한다.

items.stem: (A)~(E) 중 <보기>에 주어진 문장의 위치로 가장 적절한 곳은?

box.title: <보기>
lines: I want you to help me as soon as possible.

items.explain:
주어진 문장 "I want you to help me as soon as possible."은 문제를 설명한 뒤 도움을 요청하는 말이므로, "I don't know what the problem is or what to do." 다음이자 "I hope to hear from you soon." 앞인 (D)가 알맞다.
원문 순서: I don't know what the problem is or what to do. I want you to help me as soon as possible. I hope to hear from you soon.
items.source: L6 Present Your Ideas — In Writing 이메일
wrong: ① 헤드폰을 샀다는 말도 하기 전에 도움을 요청한다.
② 문제를 말하기 전에 도움을 요청한다.
③ 문제를 다 설명하기 전이라 이르다.
⑤ 답장을 기다린다는 맺음말 뒤에 오면 흐름이 어긋난다.

choices: I wonder when will start the movie.
I don't know who did call me last night.
Tell me what day is it today.
I'm not sure if we have homework.
Do you believe why he is right?
items.explain: ④ "I'm not sure if we have homework."는 의문사가 없는 간접의문문으로 「if + 주어 + 동사」 어순이 옳다.
items.source: 학습지 p.10 B-3·B-4 · 통합본 L5 p.29 14번
wrong: ① when will start the movie → when the movie will start.
② who did call me → who called me(의문사가 주어일 때는 그대로).
③ what day is it today → what day it is today.
⑤ believe 가 있으면 의문사가 문장 앞으로: Why do you believe he is right?

lines: no_more

Hi, I'm Jihun. Last month, I saw an interesting advertisement online. It said that I could get a new smartphone for free. I clicked on it without ⓐ<u>thinking</u> much. Then, I filled out my information to receive the gift. However, instead of getting a new smartphone, I have received useless emails and phone calls from unknown numbers. Oh, my! I just heard my phone ⓑ<u>to ring</u> again. It makes me very ⓒ<u>upset</u>. I'm sure that someone is using my information in a bad way. I think that my personal information ⓓ<u>was shared</u>. I want to delete it. Can you help me, please?
Happy_Digital_Laundry

We checked your online records and found the ad. Then, we asked the ad company ⓔ<u>to delete</u> your information, and they did. To protect your personal information, don't click on ads or links from unknown sources. It can be very dangerous.

items.explain:
[지문 요지] Jihun은 무료 스마트폰 광고를 눌러 정보를 입력했다가 쓸모없는 이메일과 전화에 시달리며 개인정보 삭제를 부탁하고, Happy Digital Laundry는 광고 회사에 삭제를 요청해 처리했다고 답한다.
「지각동사 hear + 목적어 + 동사원형/-ing」이므로 ⓑ to ring 은 ringing(또는 ring)이어야 한다. "I just heard my phone ringing again."
나머지는 옳다: ⓐ without thinking(전치사 + 동명사), ⓒ makes me upset(형용사 보어), ⓓ was shared(수동태), ⓔ asked the ad company to delete(ask + 목적어 + to부정사).
wrong: ① 전치사 without 뒤 동명사 thinking 으로 옳다.
③ upset 은 형용사 보어로 옳다.
④ 정보는 공유되는 대상이므로 수동태가 옳다.
⑤ ask + 목적어 + to부정사로 옳다.

box.title: <보기>
lines: What did Happy Digital Laundry do for Jihun?

choices: Happy Digital Laundry ignored Jihun's request and took no action.
Happy Digital Laundry asked the ad company to delete his information.
Happy Digital Laundry clicked on ads or links from unknown sources.
Happy Digital Laundry requires customers to come to its office to get their help.
Happy Digital Laundry completely erased every copy from all devices.
items.explain:
질문: Happy Digital Laundry는 Jihun을 위해 무엇을 했는가?
본문 "Then, we asked the ad company to delete your information, and they did."에서 광고 회사에 정보 삭제를 요청했다. ②.
items.source: L6 본문 4대목 Laundry 답장 2 · 통합본 L6 p.38 T/F
wrong: ① 요청을 무시하지 않고 기록을 확인해 조치했다.
③ 광고를 누르지 말라고 당부한 쪽이지 누른 것이 아니다.
④ 사무실 방문을 요구한 내용은 없다.
⑤ 모든 기기에서 사본을 지웠다는 내용은 Bella의 사례와도 다르고 이 글에 없다.

lines: Are you worried about your digital footprint? Do you want to erase it? If you do, visit Happy Digital Laundry. We can clean your online history. Leave a message on our website, and we'll help you soon.
remove_all_plz

Hi, I'm Bella. Last Friday, I saw my brother playing basketball after school. He was playing really well, so I took a picture of him. Then I shared ⓐ<u>it</u> on my social media. Over the weekend, something went wrong. Someone made a copy of the picture with bad comments. The copy was spread here and there, and I was so embarrassed. My brother wanted me to delete the picture of him. I apologized to him, and I deleted my post immediately. ______________(A)______________ I want to remove them all. Please help me.

choices: Bella saw her brother playing basketball last Friday.
Bella was so impressed by her brother's basketball game that she took a picture of him.
Something went wrong over the weekend.
Bella's brother made a copy of the picture with bad comments.
Bella felt sorry for her brother for what happened with the picture.
items.explain:
[지문 요지] Happy Digital Laundry 광고와, 오빠의 농구 사진을 올렸다가 나쁜 댓글이 달린 사본이 퍼져 도움을 청하는 Bella의 글이다.
본문 "Someone made a copy of the picture with bad comments."에서 사본을 만든 것은 '누군가'이지 Bella의 오빠가 아니다. ④는 틀리다.
items.source: L6 본문 1대목 Bella · 통합본 L6 p.38 T/F · 실전모의고사 21번
wrong: ① Last Friday, I saw my brother playing basketball 과 일치한다.
② He was playing really well, so I took a picture of him. 과 일치한다.
③ Over the weekend, something went wrong. 과 일치한다.
⑤ I apologized to him. 에서 미안해했음을 알 수 있다.

choices: the picture of him
her social media
basketball
the copy
the school
items.explain: "I took a picture of him. Then I shared it on my social media."에서 it 은 바로 앞에서 찍은 the picture of him(오빠의 사진)을 가리킨다.
wrong: ② social media 는 사진을 올린 곳이다.
③ basketball 은 오빠가 하던 운동이다.
④ the copy 는 뒤에 나온다.
⑤ the school 은 언급되지 않는다.

choices: However, the copies still remain online.
So, the copies still remain online.
Someone made a copy of the picture with bad comments.
Over the weekend, something went wrong.
My article was posted online.
items.explain: "I apologized to him, and I deleted my post immediately."(게시물을 즉시 지웠다) 뒤에 "I want to remove them all."(그것들을 모두 지우고 싶다)이 오므로, 지웠는데도 사본이 여전히 남아 있다는 반대 흐름의 ① "However, the copies still remain online."이 알맞다. them 이 가리킬 the copies 도 이 문장에 있다.
wrong: ② So 는 인과인데, 지웠기 때문에 남아 있다는 것은 모순이다.
③ 사본이 만들어졌다는 문장은 이미 앞에 나왔다.
④ 주말에 일이 생겼다는 문장도 이미 앞에 나왔다.
⑤ 기사 게시는 Ms. Ali의 이야기이다.

lines: Reporter: I want to know why you ⓐ<u>wanted</u> to be a sports statistician, Ms. Lee.
Ms. Lee: I wanted to be a sports statistician because I liked ⓑ<u>analyze</u> sports with numbers. (A)<u>Above all, I love ice hockey.</u>
Reporter: I don't know much about a sports statistician. Can you explain it to me?

Ms. Lee: (B)<u>A sports statistician is someone ⓒ<u>who</u> collects data and studies numbers about sports games.</u> (C)<u>Our team is going to play against the Ice Lions this Saturday.</u> Last week, I carefully watched the Ice Lions' games and analyzed their shots. (D)<u>I prefer team sports to individual sports.</u> I found ⓓ<u>that</u> they let in 70 percent of the shots from the left side. This showed their left side was weak. (E)<u>Then, I shared this finding with our players.</u> I'm happy ⓔ<u>to use</u> my data to help our team.

items.stem: (A)~(E) 중 글의 흐름상 전체적인 내용과 어울리지 <u>않는</u> 것은?
items.explain:
[지문 요지] 스포츠 통계 전문가 Ms. Lee가 숫자로 스포츠를 분석하며 Ice Lions의 약점을 찾아 선수들과 공유한 이야기이다.
(D) "I prefer team sports to individual sports."(개인 운동보다 팀 운동을 더 좋아한다)는 Ice Lions의 슛 분석 이야기 사이에 끼어 흐름을 끊는다.
items.source: L5 본문 3대목 Ms. Lee (무관 문장은 L5 LT-A3에서 가져옴 — 일부러 넣은 문장)
wrong: ① 이 일을 택한 이유에 덧붙인 문장으로 흐름에 맞는다.
② 통계 전문가가 무엇인지 설명하는 문장으로 흐름에 맞는다.
③ 상대팀과의 경기를 알리는 문장으로 흐름에 맞는다.
⑤ 발견을 선수들과 공유했다는 문장으로 흐름에 맞는다.

items.explain:
like 는 to부정사나 동명사를 목적어로 취하므로 ⓑ analyze 는 to analyze(또는 analyzing)여야 한다. "I liked to analyze sports with numbers."
나머지는 옳다: ⓐ why you wanted(간접의문문 어순, 과거), ⓒ someone who collects(주격 관계대명사), ⓓ found that(목적어절 접속사), ⓔ happy to use(감정의 원인).
wrong: ① 간접의문문 why you wanted 로 옳다.
③ 선행사 someone 을 받는 주격 관계대명사 who 로 옳다.
④ found 의 목적어절을 이끄는 that 으로 옳다.
⑤ I'm happy to use 는 '~해서 기쁘다'로 옳다.

choices: Why did Ms. Lee want to be a sports statistician?
What does a sports statistician do?
When is Ms. Lee's team going to play against the Ice Lions?
How many players are on the Ice Lions?
What did Ms. Lee find about the Ice Lions' left side?
items.explain: ④ Ice Lions에 선수가 '몇 명' 있는지는 글에 나오지 않는다.
wrong: ① because I liked to analyze sports with numbers — 답할 수 있다.
② someone who collects data and studies numbers about sports games — 답할 수 있다.
③ this Saturday — 답할 수 있다.
⑤ their left side was weak — 답할 수 있다.

lines: There was a big basketball game between the Boston Wolves and the Miami Monsters. The game ____ⓐ____ at the Boston Sports Center on September 2. The Boston Wolves won the game by 10 points. Michael James played his best game of the season against the Monsters. His perfect play made his team and his fans ____ⓑ____. Everyone is looking forward to his next game.

items.explain:
ⓐ 경기는 '열리는' 대상이고 on September 2 라는 과거이므로 was held, ⓑ 「make + 목적어 + 형용사」에서 팀과 팬이 신나는 감정을 느끼므로 excited.
원문: "The game was held at the Boston Sports Center on September 2. … His perfect play made his team and his fans excited."
items.source: L5 Present Your Ideas — Sports News
wrong: ② held 는 능동으로 경기가 무언가를 개최했다는 뜻이 된다.
③ exciting 은 사람이 느끼는 감정에 쓰지 않는다.
④ held 는 능동이고 excitedly 는 부사라 보어가 될 수 없다.
⑤ was holding 은 진행형 능동이다.

choices: 민수: There was a big baseball game between the Boston Wolves and the Miami Monsters.
지호: The Miami Monsters won the game by 10 points.
수아: The Boston Wolves won the game by 10 points.
하은: Michael James played his best game of the season against the Wolves.
준서: Nobody is looking forward to his next game.
items.explain:
[지문 요지] Boston Wolves가 Miami Monsters를 10점 차로 이겼고 Michael James가 시즌 최고의 경기를 펼쳤다는 기사이다.
③ 수아: 본문 "The Boston Wolves won the game by 10 points."와 그대로 일치한다.
items.source: L5 Present Your Ideas — Sports News
wrong: ① 민수: baseball 이 아니라 basketball 경기이다.
② 지호: 이긴 팀은 Monsters 가 아니라 Wolves 이다.
④ 하은: against the Monsters 이지 Wolves 가 아니다.
⑤ 준서: Everyone is looking forward to his next game.
